original_value: SummaryCiphertext‐policy attribute‐based encryption (CP‐ABE) is regarded as one of the most suitable technologies for data access control in cloud storage system. It gives data owners direct and flexible control on access policies. However, there still exists practicality concerns in CP‐ABE applications, for example, the key escrow problem, user revocability, and large ciphertext size. Considering these problems, we propose a multi‐authority attribute‐based encryption scheme with constant‐size ciphertexts and user revocation for threshold access policy in this paper. The security proof shows that the proposed scheme is selectively secure under the augmented multi‐sequence of exponents decisional Diffie‐Hellman assumption, and it also achieves forward security, backward security, and collusion‐resistance.

result.paraphrase: Ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption (CP-ABE) is considered one of the most suitable technologies for data access control in cloud storage systems. It provides data owners with direct and flexible control over access policies. However, CP-ABE still has practical concerns, such as the key escrow problem, user revocation, and large ciphertext size. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-authority attribute-based encryption scheme with constant-size ciphertexts and user revocation for threshold access policies. The security proof shows that the proposed scheme is selectively secure under the augmented multi-sequence of exponents decisional Diffie-Hellman assumption, and it also provides forward security, backward security, and collusion resistance.
